newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends down in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends down in quiet trade.

text.p: Indian call money ended Monday at 5.0-5.25 percent in quiet trade after opening higher at 5.5-6.0 percent, dealers said.
Good supply of funds and moderate demand kept rates within a narrow band with most deals done between 5.25 poercent and 5.5 percent, they said.
"At the moment, liquidity with the banking system is good," said a dealer at a private bank. "Given that demand is also not very high, I fell call money rates will hover around the repos rates."
Repos auctions of government of India securities by the Reserve Bank of India during February have been at 5.0 percent.
"Further the repos are of three- or four-day maturities," the dealer said. "This means that funds going out come back in a short time and banks have more investment options."
Dealers said prices of government securities were mixed in moderate trade.
"Today's trades were worth about 1.12 billion rupees against Saturday's one billion," said a money market dealer.

The 13.65 percent 1998 government of India stock traded on Monday at 102.47 rupees against its last traded price of 102.53, the 13.50 percent 1998 stock at 103.0 against 103.02, 13.70 percent 1999 stock at 101.70 against 101.65, dealers said.
